name: Huessen EPF1301 13.3 inch frame
description: 13.3 inch Spectra 6 E Ink picture frame (EL133UF1, 1200x1600 portrait glass hung landscape) on an ESP32-S3 with 16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM, a Li-ion cell and native USB. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API from the tesserae-device-firmware build (env huessen-epf1301) and paints the esp32_bin 4-bpp Spectra 6 frame, the same 960000-byte wire format as the reTerminal E1004.
notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware by the firmware's contributor (tesserae-device-firmware PR #54, 2026-10-28): self-test colour bars on both controller halves, the captive portal, registration and server frames. A healthy full refresh takes about 19 s; the firmware cycles the display rail around every paint, as the stock firmware does.

Wire format is exactly 960000 bytes (1200*1600/2), row-major from the top-left of the portrait framebuffer, high nibble = left pixel, Spectra 6 controller codes (0 black, 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 red, 5 blue, 6 green). The firmware registers with rotation 0 and turns nothing on the device, so a landscape dashboard is turned onto the portrait buffer by the server; set the device's orientation in Settings -> Devices for the way the frame hangs.

Not auto-selected from a relay self-report: on the wire it is indistinguishable from the other 1200x1600 Spectra 6 kinds, so it is only ever set by the firmware declaring it at register / discover, or by the operator.

The first USB flash replaces the stock firmware, bootloader included; take a full flash backup first (`esptool.py --chip esp32s3 read_flash 0 0x1000000 huessen-stock.bin`). The panel runs off the battery rail, so the cell has to be fitted even on USB. The GPIO1 key wakes the frame and acts as Refresh.
